summary.intent: Drive Caliper toward a v1 alpha by creating and executing six Entire trails (comparison, perf, detection, recall, types, release flow), then follow-on work: making the tsrs checker the default and keeping Caliper at least 2-3x faster than react-docgen-typescript.
summary.outcome: Trails 153-158 were created and workers produced stacked draft PRs (#280-#283 for oracle/weekly, #441 checker-default, #442 weekly on checker). The #440 leak fix was verified in code. The trail 154 perf branches and trail 158 release-flow worker report are not yet pushed. The checker extract speed worker crashed on an API error and was resumed, with no RDT-vs-checker numbers yet.

repo: Nothing in the repo defined 'v1 alpha'; the user supplied a plan file outside the repo at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md.

Workflow is trails before branches: workers commit locally and GPG-sign; the coordinator pushes, links with `entire trail link --base <parent>` before any PR exists, then edits PR titles/bodies keeping the Entire marker.
Stacked branches cannot share a parent, so oracle/three-tools-report needs both weekly and oracle stacks merged first.
Callisto is already at latest (0.16.0 per research; CI uses 0.20.0). Release v0.9.0 published tags only, with no GitHub Releases because callisto.toml lacks `github-release` in publish-to.

Callisto's attestation check expects a signer workflow named `callisto-release.yml`, so release.yml likely needs renaming (unverified in source). Product package must be a Cargo package (cargo/caliper-docgen) because an npm bin can't be an artifact product (E304).
The Homebrew tap reads tag npm/caliper-docgen@x.y.z, so tag-template should stay unset.
Release run failure E148 was a stale release-PR snapshot race in the version-pr step; a re-run or next push fixes it and nothing was lost.
react-docgen's default importer follows imports (the old 'reads each file alone' docs claim was wrong), and it throws on 17-21% of files in antd and shadcn.
antd recall reached 92.1% (186/202), short of the ~95% target; the remaining unpaired items are factories, compound members and the like, not pairing cases.
The checker default costs about 6 s and ~970 MiB on gate-large (938 components) versus 0.09-0.10 s with --no-checker; the 17-39x speed claim over RDT is now only valid for --no-checker.
The Storybook addon is already structural-first with the checker answering within semanticWaitMs (150 ms) and prefetches the first story, but lacks a live upgrade of an open story.
Sessions held a copy of every prop per checker answer (~6.7 MiB per component); AnswerCache::shared in core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs fixes it.
UNIVERSE_VERSION in scripts/weekly.py was bumped to 5 to avoid a false 'wrong types rose' issue when the weekly switched to the checker.

code.finding: A refused createSnapshot/updateSnapshot response now calls discard() to release the snapshot the answer created; previously the ID was dropped and the snapshot leaked. A timed-out caller's snapshot is released near line 446.
BUDGETS for the five weekly corpora are set to {'ms': None, 'rss_mib': None} ('record on first run'); a run over a None budget opens no issue.
AnswerCache::shared dedupes identical props across checker answers and resets when session answers are dropped on a source change.

workflow: Sandbox denies writes to the job tmp dir and ~/.local/share/entire (Brain lock); use $TMPDIR instead. `tsx` fails on its IPC socket under the sandbox, so use `node` (type stripping).
The permission classifier blocked `entire trail finding resolve` as an external write; the user must run it or authorize it.
Peer and subagent messages are not user approval; the coordinator verified remote SHAs with git ls-remote before linking.
Machine load of 5-21 made timing noisy; compare only interleaved runs measured side by side.
A user /stop on a subagent restarted it from the transcript; a later API outage failed it, so workers should commit and push early.
